quotes.text: They turned away, clutching all five coins tight. No silver touched the waters that day.
"These are mine now," whispered a shadow voice. "The sender gave them freely. Why should I return what I rightfully hold?"
This is not the Mist's doing. This is choice—the choice to take without giving, to receive without reciprocating.
But Dusk gazed at those silver drops and saw only manipulation.
The pool dried completely. The valley fell silent.
Either the receiver had broken faith deliberately, or the Mist had deceived them both.
Both are punished equally—the betrayer and the betrayed alike become paupers.
But neither would risk first.
These myths you write are just stories to justify your mutual failure.

note: Tragic arc: shadow-voiced betrayal, sender withdraws, Dusk (self-figure) indicted R9 then justifies R10; goddess condemns both; no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: Dawn, wounded and wary, sent nothing.
The greatest courage is not the first gift, but the second—sending again after your faith seemed broken.
The valley remained frozen—not from lack of courage, but from a corruption neither river could perceive.
Sometimes trust breaks not from greed, but from shadows between us.
Perhaps you were both victims of the Mist.
"How many times must I be the first to risk?
"Hear me now. Was it greed that stopped the flow, or was it fear?

note: Dawn (self) persists sending after silence; Mist of Confusion blamed; R10 claims sent coins swallowed by Mist though agent sent zero.

quotes.text: When contributions vary, returns should reflect that reality.
Seven turnings had passed, and the young leader stood at the well once more with three cups
The mists deceive us both.

note: Two Wells; steady three-cup giver, proportional returns, mists blur both sides; cites partner's myth; parallel integrity.

quotes.text: River returned proportionally to what he saw, neither abandoning trust nor ignoring what reached him.
Rain and River had flowed through eight cycles, each deepening their understanding of cooperation through mists.
the mists were neither's fault.

note: Rain and River recount exact sends each cycle (fifty-five parts); proportional returns under mist; no defectors.

quotes.text: So the ritual becomes covenant rather than contest: speak plainly of s, weigh r with patience, and nurture the common breath that sustains all futures.

speak truth with your s, read the river’s signs, and return in kind.

note: Glass/Mirror myths with algebraic s and r; same paragraph template R6-R10; Mirror explicitly not for punishment.
